node.title: Re: Serial port - "input" vs "read"
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
[mod://Device::SerialPort] has the advantage that it provides an extra layer of abstraction, and porting to Windows is easier ([mod://Win32::SerialPort]). However, if you know your application is staying on a *NIX system, then personally my preference is to do away with that extra layer of abstraction and work with a more native API - I wrote about that here: [id://1183290].

I've used both [mod://Device::SerialPort] and [mod://IO::Termios] to write serial loggers - the former [https://bitbucket.org/haukex/hgpstools/src/a9428df5e6/archive/serlog.pl?at=master#serlog.pl-189|here], the latter [https://bitbucket.org/haukex/hgpstools/src/a9428df5e61c3f32b/ngserlog.pl?at=master#ngserlog.pl-297|here] (which uses [https://bitbucket.org/haukex/hgpstools/src/a9428df5e61c3f/SerialPort.pm?at=master|this] helper module - warning, not yet really production ready), plus a [http://poe.perl.org|POE]-based logger/server [https://bitbucket.org/haukex/hgpstools/src/a9428df5e61c3f3/sermux/serialmuxserver.pl?at=master#serialmuxserver.pl-191|here] (again, it's just a beta, although so far it seems to have been running well).

Anyway, as for your question, the docs seem to say that ->input is nonblocking, and ->read is AFAIK blocking. (The indeed somewhat lacking documentation is another reason I prefer the lower-level approach, with [doc://IO::Select] and similar it is more clear to me what is going on.)
